subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures remain accepted asynchronous runs that terminalize with a typed startup failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup and reject before returning accepted?
rationale: Both shapes can address the user-visible hang, but the choice affects gateway accepted semantics, subagent registry state, agent.wait behavior, and the overlapping startup lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted async spawn contract, but emit/log a typed startup failure and prove registry, session UI, and wait callers see it for Docker sandbox startup failures.

options.title: Preflight before accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation ahead of the accepted response to fail fast, accepting the latency and compatibility implications for existing callers.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle issue
options.body: Treat this issue as blocked on the broader lifecycle contract and keep it as the sandbox-specific proof case.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted async spawn contract, but emit/log a typed startup failure and prove registry, session UI, and wait callers see it for Docker sandbox startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans subagent lifecycle and terminal state semantics where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
